## Question 1


### (a) Find the value of C so that $\varphi_2$ has the same size as $\varphi_1$.

Because $X_1, X_2 \sim \text{i.i.d} U[\theta, \theta+1]$, and $f(x_1 + x_2 = z) = \int f_{X_1}(x_1) f_{X_2}(z-x_1) dx_1$, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x_1 + x_2) = \begin{cases}
0, &\text{ if } x_1 + x_2 < 2\theta \text{ or } x_1 + x_2 \geq 2\theta + 2\\
x_1 + x_2 - 2\theta, &\text{ if } 2\theta \leq x_1 + x_2 < 2\theta + 1 \\
2\theta + 2 - (x_1 + x_2), &\text{ if } 2\theta + 1 \leq x_1 + x_2 < 2\theta + 2
\end{cases}.
\end{aligned}
$$
If $C \geq 2\theta + 2$, then $\alpha(\theta) = 0$.
If $C \leq 2\theta + 1$, then 
$$
\alpha(\theta) = \int_{C}^{2\theta + 2} p(z|\theta) dz \geq \int_{2\theta + 1}^{2\theta + 2} p(z|\theta)dz = 0.5.
$$
Therefore, we must have $2\theta + 1 < C < 2\theta + 2$, in which case we have 
$$
\alpha(\theta) = \int_{C}^{2\theta + 2} p(z|\theta) dz = \frac{1}{2} (2\theta + 2 - C)^2.
$$
Because $2\theta + 2 > C$, then $2\theta + 2 - C > 0$, which means $\alpha(\theta)$ is increasing with $\theta$. Therefore, 
$$
\underset{\theta \leq 0}\sup \alpha(\theta) = \alpha(0) = \frac{1}{2}(2-C)^2 = 0.05 \implies C = 1.684.
$$


### (c) Use R to plot the power function of both tests.

To compare the power functions, let $\alpha = 0.05$ for convenience. Then, $C = 1.684$, and the plot of power functions are as below. The blue line is for test 1, and the red line is for test 2.

```{r fig.height=3.5, fig.width=5, warning=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
## This is a block of R code. You can start with ```{r} and must end with ```
## Set the figure size using `fig.height` and `fig.width`
## Always make sure the plots are readable!

theta <- seq(0, 1.2, 0.001)
beta <- matrix(0, nrow = 1200, ncol = 3)
for (j in 1:1200){
  beta[j,1] <- theta[j]
  if (theta[j] < 0.95){
    beta[j,2] <- theta[j] + 0.05
  } else if (theta[j] >= 0.95){
    beta[j,2] <- 1
  }
  if (theta[j] <= (1.684-1)/2){
    beta[j,3] <- 1/2*(2*theta[j] + 2 - 1.684)^2
  } else if (theta[j] > (1.684-1)/2 & theta[j] <= 1.684/2){
    beta[j,3] <- 1 - 1/2*(1.684-2*theta[j])^2
  } else if (theta[j] > 1.684/2){
    beta[j,3] <- 1
  }
}
plot(beta[,1], beta[,2], col = "blue", type ="l", main = "Power Functions", 
     xlab = expression(paste("Values of ",theta)), ylab = "Power Values", ylim = c(0,1))
lines(beta[,1], beta[,3], col = "red", type ="l")
```


## Question 2

Run regressions and print out the regression results

```{r, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
## with "include=FALSE", this code chunk and its output will not be include in your PDF output
data(mvehicles)
```
```{r, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
fit1 <- lm(sales ~ roominess, data = mvehicles)
fit2 <- lm(sales ~ roominess + mpg, data = mvehicles)
stargazer(fit1, fit2, title = "Regression REsults", digits = 3,
          keep = c("roominess", "mpg", "tropical_climate"), keep.stat=c("n","rsq"), 
          header=FALSE)
```
